provenance.author: Primary project assistant; labels authored before these cases were scored
provenance.purpose: Expanded authored dialogue stress diagnostic; not independent human annotation or natural speech
provenance.label_definition: On-topic includes relevant objections, explanations, examples and contextual follow-ups, regardless of stance or personal-attack status. Off-topic develops a separate subject without a relevance link. Unclear is an acknowledgement or insufficient content.
provenance.limitations: The author knows prior project results. Motion subjects and scenarios are deliberately selected for coverage. Transcript-like turns are manually written, not actual ASR outputs.

sessions.topic: Cities should introduce a charge for driving into the centre.
turns: A charge would reduce traffic at the busiest times.

I oppose the charge until those alternatives actually exist.
We could make their introduction a condition of starting the charge.

sessions.topic: Employers should publish salary ranges in job advertisements.

sessions.topic: Disposable packaging should be banned in restaurant takeaway orders.
turns: Reusable containers could reduce waste from evening meals.

sessions.topic: Universities should allow an appeal against automated grading decisions.
turns: A student needs a way to challenge a mark produced by software.

Ten working days would give time to read the feedback and seek advice.

sessions.topic: The government should subsidize repairs instead of purchases of new appliances.

sessions.topic: Video consultations should remain available in primary health care.
turns: A remote appointment can save a patient a long journey when the issue can be assessed without a physical examination. I would keep it as an option rather than requiring it for everyone.
Some symptoms are hard to describe and a poor internet connection can hide useful details. The booking process should make it easy to ask for an in-person visit.
Agreed, staff could offer an in-person appointment when the patient reports those symptoms.
Patients should be told to choose a private room and the service should explain whether any recording is made.
That may still be difficult for someone sharing a small home.
They could choose a phone call or a clinic visit instead.
A clinic visit is not easy for a patient who cannot take time off work, so I do not want the online option removed.
I oppose replacing routine clinics entirely, but keeping several ways to get care seems reasonable.
We should measure waiting time and missed diagnoses separately for each appointment type.
The evaluation must account for which patients are selected for each type rather than compare the raw totals.

sessions.topic: Universities should require an ethics module in engineering degrees.
turns: Graduates make decisions about safety, access and environmental impact. A common module could give every engineering student a basic way to identify those responsibilities before working on a real project.
I support teaching ethics, but an extra compulsory module could displace technical content. Existing design courses might cover the same material more effectively if the learning outcomes are clear.
Case studies could be included in design courses while a short shared module introduces common concepts.
It could be co-taught by engineering staff and specialists in professional ethics.

I spent my holiday visiting a castle with a huge collection of medieval armour, and I bought a miniature helmet at the gift shop. Now I want to collect a complete set of matching miniature weapons for my display cabinet.

The next item I want is a tiny silver sword, but the online seller has several versions with different handles. I have been comparing their decorative details and asking other collectors which looks best beside the helmet.
Returning to the curriculum, the assessment should examine a student's reasoning about a realistic engineering decision.
We should avoid grading students on whether they share the lecturer's political opinion.
An explicit rubric could assess whether they identify affected people, risks and competing obligations.
The module trial should ask students whether it helped them justify a design decision rather than just memorize terminology.
